draft.shortGloss: to put; to turn on; to put on; to get
draft.emotion: helpful and practical, getting things where they need to go
notes: Irregular in the present first-person singular (pongo), the preterite (puse, pusiste...), and the past participle (puesto).
Used reflexively (ponerse) for putting on clothes and for a change of state or mood (ponerse nervioso).

senses.definition: To place something in a specific location.

examples.text: Voy a poner las llaves sobre la mesa.
examples.translation: I am going to put the keys on the table.
examples.emotion: focused and direct, organizing things in the room

senses.definition: To make an appliance, light, or broadcast start working or playing.

examples.text: Puedes poner la televisión para ver las noticias.
examples.translation: You can turn on the television to watch the news.
examples.emotion: casual and inviting, relaxing in the evening

senses.definition: (reflexive, ponerse) To dress yourself in an item of clothing.

examples.text: Hace frío, ponte un abrigo antes de salir.
examples.translation: It is cold, put on a coat before going out.
examples.emotion: caring and attentive, looking out for someone

senses.definition: (reflexive, ponerse) To begin to be in a particular state, mood, or condition.

examples.text: Siempre se pone nervioso antes de un examen.
examples.translation: He always gets nervous before an exam.
